description: WireGuard overlay addressing. This file is the single source of truth for the overlay network. Both the Master and every peer read these values; neither role hard-codes them.

reserved_peer_addresses.10.100.0.1: the Master Anchor — never assignable to a peer
reserved_peer_addresses.10.100.0.255: broadcast — never assignable to a peer

peer_allowed_ips_rule: A peer's [Peer] AllowedIPs must cover exactly one address: 10.100.0.1/32 for the Master edge, or the peer's own single /32 on a Master-side stanza. Wider masks permit source-spoofing a sibling.

governance_mode.purpose: Decides who arbitrates a cross-node share. It is determined by the node count in the signed registry, never by local configuration, so a node cannot opt itself out of review.
governance_mode.determined_by: count of non-revoked entries in the signed registry (manifests/node-authorizations.json)

solo.rule: No cross-node share exists. Isolation means the node's own external data path only; the Master edge stays up so evidence and revocation remain reachable.

peer_pair.rule: Symmetric. No Master arbitration is available or required: the two members verify shared information against their existing knowledge base instead. The Master does not interpose on their share, and a Master outage does not interrupt it. One member may be the elected Master — its operational key governs authority-plane messages only (registry, approval, 10.100.0.1/32) and still does not arbitrate this pair's shares.
peer_pair.peer_pair_rationale: Requiring a Master in a two-node mesh would give the Master a veto over data the Master cannot review on both sides, and would make the smallest useful deployment depend on a third party.

master_governed.rule: The Master arbitrates every cross-node share, including peer-to-peer ones. Ratification is required for a share to survive its window.

governance_mode.re_evaluation: The mode is recomputed from the registry on every share request, so a third node joining mid-share re-evaluates that share rather than grandfathering it under the rules it was created under. A share already created under peer_pair is not retroactively ratified by the arrival of a third node; it ends, and may be re-offered under the new mode.
governance_mode.authority_consequence: governance_mode never widens the authority plane. In every mode the peer-to-Master AllowedIPs rule above is unchanged, and only the arbitration of shares changes.

data_plane_stanza.purpose: Carry time-boxed peer-to-peer traffic that is deliberately outside the authority plane: cross-node conversation passing and share transport.
data_plane_stanza.why_separate: The authority plane is the path a node trusts to carry signed instructions, and its AllowedIPs rule admits exactly one address. Widening it to reach a sibling would let any sibling-present a source address the node believes is the Master, which is the exact confusion the single-address rule exists to prevent. Peer-to-peer traffic therefore rides a distinct construct whose trust basis is a share grant, not a key held by the peer itself.
data_plane_stanza.trust_basis: a signed, unexpired, unrevoked share grant naming the counterpart node's fingerprint — never the mere fact that a packet arrived from an overlay address.
constraints: A data-plane stanza exists only for the lifetime of a share grant and is torn down when it expires, is revoked, hits its idle timeout, or its overlay address changes.
It grants no authority. A node reached over a data-plane stanza can be talked into nothing it could not also be talked into by its own operator.
It does not carry registry distribution, guard approval or any other authority-plane message. Those remain Master-only, 10.100.0.1/32.
Both endpoints record the stanza's open and close in the ledger, so an unlogged stanza is a detectable fault.
unverified_on_dev_host: that a data-plane stanza can be torn down on idle timeout without disturbing the authority plane
that source-address spoofing across the data plane is actually refused

mtu_rationale: Keeps the tunnel clear of the 1500-byte path MTU when the same NIC also carries ordinary TCP. The deployed AGX fleet has no RoCEv2.
teardown: Master-side revocation, or the node-local containment KillSwitch. Never a plain systemctl stop.
unverified_on_dev_host: host firewall enforcement (iptables on the deployed fleet)
